paragraphs: I am Lily, and I go to the shop with Dad and Tom. We need food for a good meal on Sunday. Dad says, "Read the labels, Lily." "A label tells you about a thing," he says. I look for the key words on each label. Tom pushes the shopping cart. I hold a small paper list. The shop is big, and it is cool inside. We do not buy sweets today.

First, we find a box of cereal. The label says, "Crunchy rice cereal. Add cold milk." "It is a good meal for the morning," says Tom. There are many kinds of cereal on the shelf. I read the label on another box too. Next, we take a small box of butter. The label says, "Butter. Keep in the fridge." "The fridge is cold, so the butter stays good," I say. We put the butter in the cart quite fast.

Then we look at curly pasta in a big bag. The label says, "Curly pasta. Cook for ten minutes." "Is ten minutes quite long?" asks Tom. "No, it is easy," says Dad. "We can talk during the cooking time." Dad takes two bags, because we are hungry. I put them in the cart. The curly pasta looks like little springs.

At the end, Tom sees a blue T-shirt. The label inside says, "Size M. Wash in cold water." "The size is right for me," says Tom. The T-shirt is soft, and he wants it for Saturday. "Wash it in cold water," I read. Dad smiles and gives money at the counter. "Now you can read every label," he says. I am very happy with my key words.
text.summary: Lily, Tom, and Dad shop for a meal. Lily reads the labels on a cereal box, butter, curly pasta, and a T-shirt, and she finds the key words.
